_comment: Octail's own egg (no upstream file). Red-DiscordBot, the self-hosted modular Discord bot: the install creates a Python virtual environment in .venv and installs the pinned Red-DiscordBot release from PyPI into it (pip checks each download against PyPI's hash). Red 3.5 needs Python 3.8-3.11, so the egg runs on the debian image with Debian 12's Python 3.11 (the installer uses the same Debian Python, so the environment matches); python_3.12 can't run it. The first start creates the instance octail (JSON storage in data/, settings in .config/) with redbot-setup --no-prompt. The bot token is write-only (secret) and reaches Red in its own RED_TOKEN environment variable, never on the command line or in a file; the start refuses to run without one. Red's console takes no input after the start (--no-prompt); it stops on Ctrl+C. The start is the 'Loaded N cogs with N commands' line Red prints once it is connected.
name: Red-DiscordBot
author: eggs@octail.net
description: Red-DiscordBot: a self-hosted, modular Discord bot (moderation, music through Lavalink, custom commands, hundreds of community cogs). The pinned release from PyPI in a virtual environment; set the bot token from Discord's Developer Portal on the Startup tab.

startup_commands.Default: export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$(pwd)/.config"; if [ -z "${RED_TOKEN}" ]; then echo '[Octail] Set Bot Token on the Startup tab (Discord Developer Portal: your application, Bot, Reset Token), then start again.'; exit 1; fi; if [ ! -x .venv/bin/python ]; then echo '[Octail] .venv is missing: reinstall the server.'; exit 1; fi; if ! grep -qs '"octail"' .config/Red-DiscordBot/config.json; then echo '[Octail] Creating the Red instance octail in data/ (first start)'; .venv/bin/python -m redbot.setup --no-prompt --instance-name octail --data-path "$(pwd)/data" --backend json || exit 1; fi; exec .venv/bin/python -m redbot octail --no-prompt --prefix "${BOT_PREFIX}" $([ -n "${OWNER_ID}" ] && printf -- '--owner %s' "${OWNER_ID}") ${RED_ARGS}

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# Red-DiscordBot installation script (Octail's own): a fresh Python virtual environment in .venv with the pinned
# Red-DiscordBot release from PyPI (pip checks each download against the hash PyPI lists, over HTTPS). Red 3.5 needs
# Python 3.8 to 3.11, so this uses Debian 12's Python 3.11, the same one the runtime image (debian) runs. The bot's data
# (data/) and its instance settings (.config/) stay on a reinstall; cogs reinstall their own requirements into data/.
# Failures exit non-zero.
#
# Server Files: /mnt/server
set -euo pipefail

VERSION="${RED_VERSION:-3.5.24}"
export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
if ! apt-get update -qq; then
    echo "Installation failed: apt couldn't read Debian's package lists."
    exit 1
fi
if ! apt-get install -y -qq --no-install-recommends python3 python3-venv > /dev/null; then
    echo "Installation failed: Debian's python3-venv couldn't be installed."
    exit 1
fi
PYTHON_VERSION=$(python3 -c 'import sys; print("%d.%d" % sys.version_info[:2])')
if [ "$PYTHON_VERSION" != "3.11" ]; then
    echo "Installation failed: the installer has Python ${PYTHON_VERSION}, the runtime image runs Debian 12's Python 3.11."
    exit 1
fi

cd /mnt/server
## a new environment every time: no packages left over from another version
rm -rf .venv
python3 -m venv .venv
echo "Installing Red-DiscordBot ${VERSION} from PyPI"
if ! .venv/bin/python -m pip install --no-cache-dir --disable-pip-version-check --root-user-action=ignore -q "Red-DiscordBot==${VERSION}"; then
    echo "Installation failed: Red-DiscordBot ${VERSION} couldn't be installed (check the version)."
    exit 1
fi
if ! INSTALLED=$(.venv/bin/python -m redbot --version); then
    echo "Installation failed: Red-DiscordBot doesn't start."
    exit 1
fi
mkdir -p data

## install end
echo "-----------------------------------------"
echo "Installation completed: ${INSTALLED}."
echo "Set Bot Token on the Startup tab before the first start."
echo "-----------------------------------------"

variables.name: Bot Token
variables.description: Your bot's token (Discord Developer Portal: your application, Bot, Reset Token). Required before the first start; never shown again once set, and never written to the server folder.

variables.name: Prefix
variables.description: The command prefix (such as ! or red.); commands are then !help and so on. No spaces or quotes.

variables.name: Owner ID
variables.description: Optional: the Discord user ID of the bot's owner. Empty: the owner of the bot's application in the Developer Portal. The owner can run every command, including ones that read the server's files: only the person hosting the bot.

variables.name: Red Version
variables.description: The Red-DiscordBot release from PyPI, such as 3.5.24. Reinstall to switch; the bot keeps its data.

variables.name: Extra Arguments
variables.description: Extra redbot flags, such as --team-members-are-owners or --mentionable.
